extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students studying algebraic topology / homotopy theory
extracted.subtask_description: A selection of exercises, theorems, definitions, and explanatory prose from a textbook section on homotopy theory connecting homotopy groups, cohomology, Eilenberg–MacLane spaces, loopspaces, and spectra. Targets both problem statements to prove and conceptual/definitional criteria needed to construct cohomology theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy equivalence criterion for n-dimensional CW complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: A map between connected n-dimensional CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence if it induces an isomorphism on π_i for all i ≤ n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint in text: Pass to universal covers and use homology.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of inclusion on top homotopy for S^n-subcomplex
rubrics_metrics.description: If an n-dimensional CW complex X contains a subcomplex Y homotopy equivalent to S^n, then the inclusion-induced map π_n(Y) → π_n(X) is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use the Hurewicz homomorphism.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Simply-connected closed 3-manifold homotopy S^3
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed simply-connected 3-manifold is homotopy equivalent to S^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Use Poincaré duality and that closed manifolds are homotopy equivalent to CW complexes; note: homeomorphism (Poincaré conjecture) is a stronger statement proved by Perelman.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed surfaces with infinite π1 are K(π,1)'s
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed surfaces whose fundamental group is infinite are K(π,1) spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show universal covers are contractible using the Hurewicz theorem and results of §3.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representability of homotopy classes by induced maps on π_n
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is (n−1)-connected CW complex and Y is path-connected with π_i(Y)=0 for i>n, then the map [X,Y] → Hom(π_n(X), π_n(Y)), sending [f] ↦ f_*, is a bijection. Deduce uniqueness (up to homotopy) of K(G,n) by G and n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the connectivity hypotheses and vanishing of higher homotopy to reduce homotopy classes to homomorphisms on π_n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wedge inclusion equivalence under relatively prime homology orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are simply-connected CW complexes such that H_i(X) and H_j(Y) are finite and have relatively prime orders for all pairs (i,j), then the inclusion X ∨ Y → X × Y is a homotopy equivalence and the smash product X ∧ Y is contractible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Use the Künneth formula.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher homotopy of powers of K(G,1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a K(G,1) CW complex, then π_n(X^n) (the n-fold product?) is free abelian for n ≥ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement as given in exercise; use properties of K(G,1) spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triviality of π1-action on higher π_n in product with K(G,1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G be a group and X a simply-connected space. For the product K(G,1) × X, the action of π_1 on π_n is trivial for all n > 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the product structure and the fact X is simply-connected to see the fundamental group action is by projection to the K(G,1) factor and is trivial on higher homotopy of the other factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing space with prescribed π_n via product of K(G_n,n)'s
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a sequence of CW complexes K(G_n,n) (n=1,2,...) and forming the union X of the finite products of the first n factors, the resulting CW complex X satisfies π_n(X) ≅ G_n for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form X as union of the nested finite products via inclusions setting nth coordinate to basepoint; compute homotopy groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing H_{n+1} of K(G,n) for n>1
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Construct a K(G,n) from a Moore space M(G,n) by attaching cells of dimension > n+1; then homology in dimension n+1 vanishes.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Hurewicz theorem to next dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is (n−1)-connected CW complex then the Hurewicz homomorphism h: π_{n+1}(X) → H_{n+1}(X) is surjective when n > 1; for n = 1 there is an isomorphism H_2(X)/im(h) ≅ π_2(X) (text gives relation to building K(π_n(X), n) and considering homology of pair).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build a K(π_n(X), n) from X by attaching cells of dimension n+2 and higher, then analyze long exact sequence of pair (Y,X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Moore space M(G,1) criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a Moore space M(G,1) with π_1 ≅ G iff H_2(K(G,1); Z) = 0. In particular, there is no M(Z^n,1) with fundamental group Z^n free abelian of rank n if n ≥ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build M(G,1) from the 2-skeleton K_2 of a K(G,1) by attaching 3-cells according to a basis for the free group H_2(K_2; Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phenomenon: same homotopy groups but not homotopy equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist finite-dimensional CW complexes X with universal cover X such that X and X × K(π_1(X),1) have isomorphic homotopy groups but are not homotopy equivalent when π_1(X) contains elements of finite order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes example of RP^2 and S^2 × RP^∞; shows difference due to π_1 torsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of π2 in relative π2 lies in center
rubrics_metrics.description: The image of the map π_2(X,x_0) → π_2(X,A,x_0) lies in the center of π_2(X,A,x_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an exercise; see §4.1 for context.

rubrics_metrics.name: No free action of Z_p × Z_p on spheres
rubrics_metrics.description: The group Z_p × Z_p (p prime) cannot act freely on any sphere S^n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: such an action would give a covering S^n → M with M closed manifold; for n>1 attach cells to build K(Z_p×Z_p,1) from M and examine H_{n+1}(K; Z_p) to reach a contradiction. (Case n=1 is elementary.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy classification criterion for lens spaces (congruence condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lens spaces L_m(l) and L_m(l') are homotopy equivalent if their defining parameters satisfy the congruence ℓ_1···ℓ_n ≡ ±k^n ℓ'_1···ℓ'_n (mod m) for some integer k (exercises give reduction and construction steps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text outlines steps: reduce to k=1 when k relatively prime to m; construct maps with controlled degree; choose integer d to obtain degree ±1 and deduce isomorphism on homotopy groups and thus homotopy equivalence (consider lifts to universal covers for i>1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize projection E→R as fiber bundle for certain E⊂R^2
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E ⊂ R^2 obtained by deleting a subspace of {0}×R, determine for which such E the projection E → R, (x,y) ↦ x, is a fiber bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise invites classifying removed subsets of the vertical line that allow local triviality of projection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splitting short exact sequences for fiber bundles with null-homotopic inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fiber bundle F → E → B where inclusion F ↪ E is homotopic to a constant, the long exact sequence of homotopy groups splits into split short exact sequences giving π_n(B) ≅ π_n(E) ⊕ π_{n-1}(F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to Hopf bundles S^3→S^7→S^4 and S^7→S^{15}→S^8 to deduce π_n(S^4) ≅ π_n(S^7) ⊕ π_{n-1}(S^3), etc., showing π_7(S^4) and π_{15}(S^8) contain Z summands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on sphere fiber bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: If S^k → S^m → S^n is a fiber bundle then necessarily k = n−1 and m = 2n−1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at the long exact sequence of homotopy groups to deduce these equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if Hopf-type bundles existed in all dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If fiber bundles S^{n−1} → S^{2n−1} → S^n existed for all n, then the groups π_i(S^n) would be finitely generated free abelian groups computable by induction and nonzero for i ≥ n ≥ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypothetical implication showing the nonexistence of such bundles in general has strong algebraic consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example of map inducing trivial homotopy/homology but not nullhomotopic
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a map pq: T^3 → S^2 (compose Hopf p: S^3→S^2 with q: T^3→S^3 collapsing complement of ball) which induces the trivial map on π_* and H_*, but is not homotopic to a constant map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise illustrating subtlety that trivial induced maps on homotopy and homology do not force nullhomotopy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient fiber bundle from quaternionic→complex projective spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The fiber bundle S^3 → S^{4n+3} → HP^n gives rise to a quotient fiber bundle S^2 → CP^{2n+1} → HP^n by factoring out the action of S^1 on S^{4n+3} by complex scalar multiplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quotienting by the circle action to produce CP^{2n+1} as quotient of S^{4n+3} and induce quotient bundle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for Whitehead product with S^1
rubrics_metrics.description: For basepoint-preserving maps f: S^1 → X and g: S^n → X with n > 1, the Whitehead product [f,g] equals ±(g − f⋅g), where f⋅g denotes the action of f on g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute Whitehead product and compare with action-induced difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triviality of Whitehead products in H-spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: All Whitehead products in a path-connected H-space are trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the H-space multiplication to homotope Whitehead constructions to trivial elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-finite generation of certain π_3 as module over group ring
rubrics_metrics.description: π_3(S^1 ∨ S^2) is not finitely generated as a module over Z[π_1(S^1 ∨ S^2)] (and generalization to π_{i+j-1}(S^1 ∨ S^i ∨ S^j) for i,j>1) by considering Whitehead products in the universal cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use universal cover computations and Whitehead products (see Example 4.52).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indeterminacy subgroup of a Toda bracket
rubrics_metrics.description: The indeterminacy of a Toda bracket ⟨f,g,h⟩ with f ∈ π^s_i, g ∈ π^s_j, h ∈ π^s_k is the subgroup f·π^s_{j+k+1} + h·π^s_{i+j+1} of π^s_{i+j+k+1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute indeterminacy in stable homotopy groups using compositions with f and h.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental relationship between cohomology and K(G,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 4.57: For every CW complex X and n>0 and any abelian group G there is a natural bijection T: [X, K(G,n)] → H^n(X; G), where T([f]) = f^*(α) for a distinguished fundamental class α ∈ H^n(K(G,n); G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof identifies a fundamental class via the Hurewicz isomorphism and uses representability; also works for pointed/nonpointed versions (with caveats at n=0,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Group structure on [X, K] via suspensions and loopspaces
rubrics_metrics.description: To give group structures on sets h(X,K) = [X,K], either X must be a suspension (or reduced suspension ΣX) or K must be a loopspace ΩL; the adjoint relation h(ΣX, K) ≅ h(X, ΩK) is central. Iterating loopspace constructions yields abelian groups for sufficiently high iterations (double loopspace yields abelian structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct sum via collapsing equatorial subspace then using wedge maps; use Ω and Σ adjunction and composition of loops to interpret sum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a sequence {K_n} to define a cohomology theory
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sequence of spaces {K_n} to define a reduced cohomology theory by h^n(X) = [X, K_n], the K_n should be (homotopy equivalent to) loopspaces and in fact iterated loopspaces: there should be weak homotopy equivalences K_n → ΩK_{n+1} so that suspension isomorphisms/long exact sequences arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This motivates definition of a (Ω-)spectrum (here called an Ω-spectrum): a sequence of CW complexes K_1, K_2, ... together with weak homotopy equivalences K_n → ΩK_{n+1} for all n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and consequence: Ω-spectrum gives reduced cohomology theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 4.58: If {K_n} is an Ω-spectrum, then the functors h^n(X) = [X, K_n] (extended to n ∈ Z) define a reduced cohomology theory on the category of pointed CW complexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The converse (every reduced cohomology theory arises from an Ω-spectrum) is Brown representability (proved in §4.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison theorem for cohomology theories with trivial coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 4.59: If h^* is an unreduced cohomology theory on CW pairs with h^n(point) = 0 for n ≠ 0, then there are natural isomorphisms h^n(X,A) ≅ H^n(X,A; h^0(point)) for all CW pairs (X,A) and all n. The analogous statement holds for homology theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses cellular chain/cochain comparison and degree arguments; shows uniqueness of ordinary (co)homology among theories with those coefficient constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additivity lemma for cohomology functors (sum of maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma 4.60: If h is a functor from pointed CW complexes to abelian groups satisfying the homotopy and wedge axioms, then for basepoint-preserving maps f,g: ΣX → K (or f,g: X → K under adjunction) we have (f + g)^* = f^* + g^* if h is covariant and (f + g)_* = f_* + g_* if h is contravariant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the decomposition ΣX ≅ X ∨ X with collapse maps and naturality to show additivity of induced maps; used to show degrees add and to compare cellular boundary maps across theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of fundamental class in H^n(K(G,n); G)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fundamental class α ∈ H^n(K(G,n); G) is given by the inverse of the Hurewicz isomorphism π_n(K(G,n)) ≅ H_n(K(G,n); Z) and represented cellularly by assigning to each n-cell the element of π_n determined by its characteristic map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the natural isomorphism T: [K, K] → H^n(K; G) the identity gives α = T(1), and for any cellular f: X→K the class T([f]) is represented by the cellular cocycle sending each n-cell to the image in G = π_n(K) of the characteristic map composed with f.
